subject: Staggered GPU onramp commitments & activation scenarios for Lyra Health
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@lyrahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staggered GPU onramp commitments & activation scenarios for Lyra Health

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Attached are three reservation structures we discussed for Lyra’s inference footprint: Minimal Guardrail, Staged Ramp, and Peak-Buffered. Short summary below and the full math is in the attached PDF (Lyra_Reserved_Options_20260922.pdf).

1) Minimal Guardrail (12 GPUs reserved)
   - Cluster footprint: 12x A5000-equivalent GPUs (single partition).
   - Use case: Proof-of-production; keeps critical SLAs for peak 3 qps/model.
   - Ramp: Immediate activation; 30% autoscale headroom for burst via on-demand.
   - Billing: Monthly reserved commitment; early termination fee scales with remaining months.

2) Staged Ramp (24 -> 72 GPUs across 6 months) 
   - Cluster footprint: start 24 GPUs, add 12 GPUs every 4 weeks for 4 stages to reach 72.
   - Use case: Gradual rollout of real-time chat + batch embeddings.
   - Min GPU guarantee (billing floor): 24 GPUs for months 1–2, 36 GPUs for months 3–4, 60 GPUs for months 5–6.
   - Activation windows: new tranche resources show within 10 business days of tranche start date.
   - Burst policy: 20% burst credits included to absorb short-term spikes (up to 72 peak).

3) Peak-Buffered (96 GPUs reserved, immediate capacity + burst pool)
   - Cluster footprint: 96 GPUs with split lanes for low-latency and throughput jobs.
   - Use case: Enterprise SLAs with multi-regional failover.
   - Ramp: immediate; recommended for teams anticipating sustained production load.

Key operational notes:
- Prefix caching and KV-sharing between models can reduce effective GPU demand by ~18–28% depending on workload; we included conservative cache uplift in the attached cost model.
- We can provide two-week staging activation (no extra charge) for smoke tests and warmup before tranche billing begins.
- For Staged Ramp we recommend milestone-based credits: a one-time onboarding credit applied when you reach 50% of committed GPUs and a smaller credit at full activation.

Next steps:
- If Staged Ramp looks closest, I’ll draft a tranche schedule aligned to your product milestones + a draft SOW for onboarding.
- If Procurement prefers a flat commitment, we’ll produce the Peak-Buffered contract with an SLA appendix.

Attaching: Lyra_Reserved_Options_20260922.pdf, SLA-exceptions-appendix.docx

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@lyrahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onramp commitments & activation scenarios for Lyra Health

Neha —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifying q's from product + procurement: 

- For the Staged Ramp, can you confirm the billing floor mechanics? If we hit month 3 and only use 28 GPUs instead of the 36 floor, do we pay for 36 or is there a pro-rated grace?
- The two-week staging: does that count toward the committed months if we take it immediately? We want warmup without accelerating billing.
- Burst credits: how are they consumed and reported? Will we be able to see burst consumption in the console and tie to cost allocation tags?

Also cc'ing procurement so they can flag any commercial blockers.

Thanks,
Samira
Director, Platform Engineering
Lyra Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@lyrahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered GPU onramp commitments & activation scenarios for Lyra Health

Hi Samira —

Answers inline: 

- Billing floor for Staged Ramp: you are billed against the min GPU guarantee for each month. If in month 3 the floor is 36 GPUs and you used 28, the invoice will reflect 36 GPUs' reserved rate. However, we offer a ‘true-up’ credit at the next tranche if sustained usage exceeds the floor in the subsequent period or if you elect to accelerate the next tranche within a 14-day window — this is documented in section 3.2 of the attached PDF.

- Two-week staging: does NOT count toward committed billing months. We treat staging as a waived-charge activation window explicitly for warmup and integration testing, provided the staging window is scheduled and used within the first tranche.

- Burst credits: these are tracked separately from reserved consumption; they show up in Console as a "burst_consumption" line item per application tag and we provide a weekly CSV export. Consumption reduces overage billing first and is reported per request-id when tracing is enabled.

Operationally, a few tradeoffs to surface: if you need consistent sub-100ms tails for chat during ramp, we recommend reserving a dedicated low-latency lane (a subset of GPUs pinned for low batch sizes). That changes the effective throughput for the remaining pool and is reflected in the attached throughput matrix.

If this matches your expectations I can: (A) send a redlineable term sheet to Procurement, (B) propose a tranche calendar with target activation dates, or (C) schedule a technical walk-through with our infra team to validate activation times.

Laura and Ben, please flag any commercial guardrails we should include in the term sheet.

Best,
Neha

From: Lyra Health Procurement <procurement@lyrahealth.com>

Hi Neha —

Procurement reviewed the Staged Ramp outline. A couple of commercial items to address before legal takes a look: 

1) Early termination: the proposed tapering fee is higher than our standard — can you provide a scale that reduces linearly after month 6?
2) Billing cadence: we prefer quarterly commitments invoiced upfront for committed GPUs rather than monthly invoices. Is that supported?
3) Audit logs: we need a documented SLA on access to token-level usage for internal compliance audits. Can we get daily exports for 90 days retention?

Also attached is a small annotated redline (SLA-exceptions-appendix.docx) with specific language requests.

Thanks —
Procurement Team

procurement@lyrahealth.com

Samira / Team —

Thanks for the procurement notes — we can do the following without requiring legal-level exceptions: 

- Early termination: provide a linear taper after month 6 (we'll add a table in the term sheet showing the monthly % of remaining fee).
- Quarterly billing: supported for committed GPU dollars; invoices issue at the start of each quarter for the upcoming quarter’s floor. We will map committed GPUs to quarterly invoice amounts in the SOW.
- Audit logs & retention: daily token-level exports for 90 days is supported as an add-on; we will include a config checklist and sample CSV format.

Next steps I propose: Neha to circulate an updated, redlineable term sheet this week; schedule a 30-min call Thurs to align on tranche dates and billing cadence.

I’ll send calendar invites after Neha confirms availability.

Best,
